units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
Rising and going to him .
You’re getting annoying, dear-boy; you’re getting demmed annoying.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Puts his hands on his shoulders .
Now, Tuppy, you’ve lost your figure and you’ve lost your character. Don’t lose your temper; you have only got one.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: My dear boy, if I wasn’t the most good-natured man in London—
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: We’d treat you with more respect, wouldn’t we, Tuppy?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Strolls away .
The youth of the present day are quite monstrous. They have absolutely no respect for dyed hair.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: LORD AUGUSTUS looks round angrily .
Mrs. Erlynne has a very great respect for dear Tuppy.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Then Mrs. Erlynne sets an admirable example to the rest of her sex. It is perfectly brutal the way most women nowadays behave to men who are not their husbands.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Dumby, you are ridiculous, and Cecil, you let your tongue run away with you. You must leave Mrs. Erlynne alone. You don’t really know anything about her, and you’re always talking scandal against her.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Coming towards him L.C.
My dear Arthur, I never talk scandal. I only talk gossip.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: What is the difference between scandal and gossip?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Oh! gossip is charming! History is merely gossip. But scandal is gossip made tedious by morality. Now, I never moralise. A man who moralises is usually a hypocrite, and a woman who moralises is invariably plain. There is nothing in the whole world so unbecoming to a woman as a Nonconformist conscience. And most women know it, I’m glad to say.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Just my sentiments, dear boy, just my sentiments.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Sorry to hear it, Tuppy; whenever people agree with me, I always feel I must be wrong.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: My dear boy, when I was your age—
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: But you never were, Tuppy, and you never will be.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Goes up C.
I say, Darlington, let us have some cards. You’ll play, Arthur, won’t you?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: No, thanks, Cecil.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: With a sigh .
Good heavens! how marriage ruins a man! It’s as demoralising as cigarettes, and far more expensive.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: You’ll play, of course, Tuppy?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Pouring himself out a brandy and soda at table .
Can’t, dear boy. Promised Mrs. Erlynne never to play or drink again.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Now, my dear Tuppy, don’t be led astray into the paths of virtue. Reformed, you would be perfectly tedious. That is the worst of women. They always want one to be good. And if we are good, when they meet us, they don’t love us at all. They like to find us quite irretrievably bad, and to leave us quite unattractively good.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Rising from R. table , where he has been writing letters .
They always do find us bad!
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: I don’t think we are bad. I think we are all good, except Tuppy.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: No, we are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Sits down at C. table .
We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars? Upon my word, you are very romantic to-night, Darlington.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Too romantic! You must be in love. Who is the girl?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: The woman I love is not free, or thinks she isn’t.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Glances instinctively at LORD WINDERMERE while he speaks .
A married woman, then! Well, there’s nothing in the world like the devotion of a married woman. It’s a thing no married man knows anything about.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Oh! she doesn’t love me. She is a good woman. She is the only good woman I have ever met in my life.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: The only good woman you have ever met in your life?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Yes!
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Lighting a cigarette .
Well, you are a lucky fellow! Why, I have met hundreds of good women. I never seem to meet any but good women. The world is perfectly packed with good women. To know them is a middle-class education.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: This woman has purity and innocence. She has everything we men have lost.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON
